chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It was so that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to mostly sit facing the Qiblah.
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) typically sit in relation to the Qiblah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the Prophet’s (PBUH) consistent orientation toward the Qiblah, a practice that underscores the spiritual centrality of the Kaaba in daily conduct. This posture reflects the integration of ritual directionality into mundane actions, reinforcing the concept of *muwajjah* (facing the divine direction) as a form of continuous devotion. It serves as a normative model for the Shia community regarding proper etiquette (*adab*) in sitting, linking physical orientation with spiritual mindfulness.
